near_miss.lead: ON rauðu gulli 'red gold' (*h1rewdh-) ~ Gk ἐρυθήματα
near_miss.why_not: Partners share only the colour root, in a medical (Thuc.) context; 'red gold' is a Germanic collocation (ON rautt gull, OE read gold) with no cognate gold+red pair in the slab partners.

near_miss.lead: night travel / 'í nótt' ~ ноћи путовати ~ νύκτ' ἄσαμεν
near_miss.why_not: Only *nokwts shared; the night+day figure is in Vuk context, not the pivot; ON 'stund og stað' is an alliterative Germanic pair with no cognate partner. Generic.

near_miss.lead: hallda vorð þessa nott 'keep watch this night' (vǫrðr < *wor-) ~ Gk ὁράω / νυκτός
near_miss.why_not: Gk ὁρῶντες is 'seeing', not keeping a watch; Greek watch phrasing (φυλακὰς ἔχειν, νύκτα φυλάσσειν) uses non-cognate words. Shared night only.

near_miss.lead: vaka með vopnum (night vigil under arms)
near_miss.why_not: Partner (MBh sun-like king) has nothing congruent; vaka ~ Skt vāja- etc. not in the passage.

near_miss.lead: rjóðum sverð í blóði 'redden sword in blood'
near_miss.why_not: Partners (Irish apples in bloom, Cato on nuts/leaves) share only bláth/folium 'bloom/leaf' ~ ON blóð by mapping; no congruent context. See search lead for Homeric ἐρυθαίνετο αἵματι.

near_miss.lead: father and mother pair (feðr né mǿðr ~ máthir ⁊ athir ~ pitṛ ... mātuḥ)
near_miss.why_not: Father+mother coordination is universal kinship language; the order and syntax differ (ON 'feðr né mǿðr', OIr mother first) and contexts (ring shown to parents / gifts of kin / return to father's house) are not a shared formula.

near_miss.lead: lie (*legh-) out during the night (ON liggja úti um nóttina ~ ORV въ ту нощь лежащю)
near_miss.why_not: Cognate *legh- + *nokwts in comparable military narrative, but 'lie (encamped) at night' is everyday narrative wording in both late prose texts; not distinctive.

near_miss.lead: þin moðer ... minum feðr ~ πατρὸς καὶ μητρὸς
near_miss.why_not: Generic kinship terms; ON is about advice given (rað gefa), Herodotus about a full brother. No shared figure.

near_miss.lead: night + sleep (um náttina ... til svefns ~ ἀΰπνους νύκτας ~ νυκτὸς ... ἐν ὕπνῳ)
near_miss.why_not: *nokwts + *swep-/*supno- co-occur everywhere; the Homeric 'sleepless nights' figure has no ON counterpart here (ON simply 'went to sleep').

near_miss.lead: tunga ~ lingua (+ þurfa ~ torpet by mapping)
near_miss.why_not: ON tunga here is a 'tongue of land' (place), Catullus' lingua torpet is the lover's tongue; þurfa/torpeo are cognate only by mapping and unrelated in use. Chance.

Name-giving formula *h1nomn dheh1- (Hitt. laman dai-, Ved. nāma dhā-, Gk ὄνομα θέσθαι) is renewed in ON by gefa; no partner in the bundle has a naming phrase, and the water-sprinkling naming is a specifically Norse rite.
Herodotus 'the most notable peoples are named (listed)' is not name-giving to a child; only *h1nomn shared.

Father+mother pair is universal; ON is legal (parents in outlawry), Homer is a boast of divine mother. AVŚ 'mātā bhūmiḥ ... pitā' (Earth mother, Parjanya father) is a different, cosmic figure. Not claimed.

near_miss.lead: vatn flytr af baðom augum 'water flows from both eyes' (weeping)
near_miss.why_not: Partners have water/flow (*wodr, *plew-) of rain and sea, not tears. Searched eye+water pairs in all branches: only ON prose (HolmPerg-4-fol 1-228:14) and OHG Augensegen, no tears idiom with *wodr elsewhere. Norse idiom.

near_miss.lead: wolf + she-wolf pair: ON ylgr ... ulfs ~ Ved. vŕ̥kaḥ ... vr̥kī́ḥ
near_miss.why_not: Exact cognate pair (*wlkwos / *wlkwih2) side by side, but the figures differ: RV has an apotropaic masc./fem. merism 'neither wolf nor she-wolf' (also RV 10.127.6 vr̥kyàm vŕ̥kam), whereas Óttarr's helmingr is a beasts-of-battle kenning ('the she-wolf got the wolf's bait'), not a coordination. Search: no other ON co-occurrence of ylgr+ulfr (same verse in AM-36-fol only); Lith. vilkė not paired. The shared item is a lexical derivational pair, not phraseology.

search_lead.cognate: ON rjóða (roðit, rjóðum) ~ Gk ἐρυθαίνω, both *h1rewdh- 'red(den)'; blood renewed (ON blóð vs Gk αἷμα); sword ON sverð/brandr vs Gk ἄορ (non-cognate)
search_lead.argument: Egill: 'we have often reddened the brand ... we redden the sword in blood'; Homer: 'as they were struck with the sword, the earth/water was reddened with blood'. Same verb root + blood instrument + sword in a battle-slaughter context. Weak: 'redden with blood' is a natural image, the object differs (weapon vs ground) and the blood word is not cognate; offered for review only.

search_lead.cognate: ON rauðr (rau-do gulli) ~ Gk ἐρυθρός, both *h1rewdh-; gold renewed (ON gull < *ǵʰl̥h₃tós vs Gk χρυσός, a Semitic loan)
search_lead.argument: 'Red gold' as a treasure/gift collocation: ON pivot offers marks of red gold as a gift; Theognis has 'red gold' tested on the touchstone, Il. 9.365 lists gold and red bronze among treasure. Germanic 'red gold' is formulaic (OE rēad gold, OHG rōtaz gold; recalled); collocates_8c shows rauðr ~ gull strongly over base rate in Germanic (35 vs 1.4 expected). The Greek attests the colour epithet of gold with the cognate adjective, the noun renewed. Weak: red is a natural description of pure gold, and Greek usage is rare (Theognis once, Homer applies it to bronze).

search_lead.cognate: ON nafn ~ Gk ὄνομα ~ Ved. nā́man- ~ Arm. anun (*h1nómn̥); the verb *dʰeh1- 'put' (Gk τίθημι, Ved. dhā-, Arm. dnem, Hitt. lāman dāi- recalled) is renewed in ON by gefa 'give'
search_lead.argument: ON 'lét sveininn vatni ausa ok nafn gefa' = naming a newborn boy. Od. 19.403-406 is the same situation: Autolykos is asked to 'put a name' on his newborn grandson (τίθεσθ' ὄνομα); Od. 18.5 'the name his mother put on him'. The name + 'put' formula is the inherited one (Hitt., Ved., Gk., Arm.); ON keeps the cognate noun in the same name-giving context with the verb renewed. Not claimed because the anchor partners in the slab lack the naming phrase and 'give a name' is a cross-linguistically common renewal.

note: Second reading of 15 flagged bundles; no claim defensible. Best lead: ON ylgr/ulfr ~ Ved. vŕ̥ka/vr̥kī́ (lexical pair, figures differ); search lead rjóða ~ ἐρυθαίνω + blood (Il. 10.484, 21.21).
